blocks.text: Houthi rebels on Thursday said a missile attack targeted the Yemeni government's interim capital of Aden.

Witnesses cited by news agencies reported several explosions and smoke rising from the area around the al-Maashiq Palace, in a rare attack on the headquarters of Yemen's internationally recognized government in the southern port city.
Yemeni Prime Minister Shaya al-Zindani and members of the government were safe, according to Yemen's Information Ministry.
The ministry statement added two members of the prime minister's security detail were killed.
Other reports, citing government officials, said 10 people were injured. It is currently unclear if the palace itself was hit, or what the extent of damage could be.
Houthi-affiliated media reported the strikes targeted "the headquarters of military operations, led by Saudi officers, at the Al-Maashiq Palace in Aden, as well as weapons depots belonging to them."
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya ​Saree said the strikes targeted what he called "Saudi ‌military operations headquarters in Aden," Reuters reported.

Yemen's civil war reignited in September as the Iran-backed Houthis launched a rapid offensive against government forces, capturing key territory along the Red Sea coast and expanding their control over swathes of territory on the Red Sea.
Since then both sides have regularly traded strikes. The Houthis have launched missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, with several killed in separate attacks on Riyadh airport.
Despite, Saudi-led coalition airstrikes and government counter-offensives, the group’s recent territorial gains have largely remained intact.

articles.title: Carney to deliver speech at federalist rally in Calgary ahead of Alberta referendum

image.caption: Carney greets students during a visit to the University of Calgary. (Ahmed Zakot/Reuters)

items: October 16Carney's day in CalgaryCarney greets students during a visit to the University of Calgary. (Ahmed Zakot/Reuters)I'm Kelsea Arnett, a reporter based in Calgary. Ahead of tonight's rally, Carney toured the city to rally Albertans to vote to stay in Canada. He shook hands with community leaders, local business owners and some eager students at the University of Calgary — including one who asked the prime minister to sign his chest. (Carney declined.)

How the pro-Canadian side is feelingAlex BoydA supporter of the pro-Canada group Forever Canadian in Calgary on Oct. 9. (Ahmed Zakot/Reuters)I'm Alex Boyd, a political affairs reporter at CBC Calgary. I'm headed to the rally tonight with the hope of chatting with as many federalist supporters as I can. We've heard again and again that separatist supporters would "crawl over broken glass" to vote (thank you to former premier Jason Kenney for popularizing that one), but I'm curious how the federalist side is feeling as we head into the final days of this campaign. There's a general sense that the energy has shifted a bit in recent weeks — the pro-Canadian side has begun to raise more money, there are more Canadian flags on cars and front lawns — but there's no question this has been an emotional debate on both sides. Into that comes the prime minister, who also happens to be an Albertan.

The final pushJennifer KeillerA pro-separation sign in the window of a cafe in Coutts, Alta., on Wednesday. (Jeff McIntosh/The Canadian Press)I'm Jen Keiller, a reporter in the Calgary newsroom. We're officially heading into the campaign home stretch, with Carney's appearances part of what will be a busy weekend of campaigning. Carney will make a campaign stop with Premier Danielle Smith Friday morning at a brewery in Red Deer. The pro-separation group Let Alberta Decide has a rally outside the legislature on Saturday afternoon.Then on Sunday, the Alberta Federation of Labour will rally in the same spot to encourage people to vote to remain.

The Canadian PressAlberta Premier Danielle Smith speaks during a news conference in Calgary on May 22. (Jeff McIntosh/The Canadian Press)Alberta Premier Danielle Smith wants citizens to vote yes to the nine provincial autonomy and immigration questions, but vote for Alberta to remain a province."Canada can still work," she said after voting. "We just need to make some changes."Polls have suggested a strong majority of Albertans want to remain in Canada, but the debate has at times been acrimonious, dividing families and neighbours.

Political leaders push for Alberta to stay a province, with advance polling well underwayThe Canadian PressAlberta NDP Leader Naheed Nenshi leaves after casting his referendum vote at an advance polling station in Calgary on Tuesday. (Jeff McIntosh/The Canadian Press)Advance voting began Tuesday and ends Saturday. Elections Alberta said the first day was a busy one, with close to 175,000 voters trekking to the polls.Michelle Gurney, a spokesperson for the agency, said Tuesday's turnout was higher than the daily average of nearly 152,000 people seen during the advance voting period in the 2023 provincial election.Elections Alberta has said it's expecting record voter turnout for the referendum, and it saw unprecedented interest in mail-in ballot requests last month.Gurney said Wednesday that nearly two-thirds of the roughly 658,000 special ballots requested have now been returned ahead of Friday's 5 p.m. deadline.Opposition NDP Leader Naheed Nenshi was among those who voted Tuesday. He encouraged Albertans to reject the United Conservative Party government's nine proposals and vote to stay in Canada.

October 15Oct. 19 referendum includes 10 questionsJohn MazerolleVoting in the Alberta referendum? Experts say do your homeworkAs Albertans prepare to vote in the upcoming referendum, experts are raising concerns over the complex and potentially confusing wording on the ballot. For The National, CBC’s Ashley Fraser breaks down the questions and how voters can prepare before heading to the polls.There are actually 10 questions being put to a vote next week, with the question of whether Alberta should remain a province of Canada or hold a second, binding referendum being No. 10.That question is being put to Albertans because Alberta Premier Danielle Smith promised a separation vote if citizens gathered the required number of citizens on a petition, which they did. The other nine questions come directly from the provincial government.Smith announced the referendum in mid-February, saying she trusts the judgment of Albertans.Five of the other questions deal with immigration, proposing that the province take more control over immigration from the federal government, limiting non-permanent residents' eligibility to public and social services and asking if voters should be required to show proof of citizenship in order to vote in a provincial election.Other questions include whether Alberta should work with the governments of other willing provinces on these changes: selecting their own justices for the King's Bench and Appeal courts; abolishing the Senate; allowing provinces to opt out of federal programs "that intrude on provincial jurisdiction such as health care, education and social services"; and giving provincial laws standing over federal laws in shared areas of jurisdiction. – With files from CBC Calgary and The Canadian Press

Carney to attend Forever Canadian rally in CalgaryJohn MazerolleCarney says Canada is 'worth fighting for' ahead of Alberta independence voteIn a video released on Thanksgiving Monday, Prime Minister Mark Carney called for national unity as Albertans prepare to vote next week in a referendum on the province's future in Canada.Prime Minister Mark Carney will be in Calgary tonight to attend a Forever Canadian rally tour days before a referendum asking Albertans if they should stay in Canada or hold another, binding referendum on separating. Forever Canadian founder Thomas Lukaszuk, who extended the invitation to Carney in a social media post on Monday, says Carney's decision to come to the rallies is a good sign for the movement."At the end of the day, Albertans would want to hear from him," Lukaszuk said. The announcement comes after Carney made a Thanksgiving address to Albertans from his alma mater in west Edmonton. In the video, he said Canada is facing threats to its economy but that in spite of them, the country is continuing to grow."Generations of Albertans helped build this country," Carney said. "It's yours, it's ours and it's worth fighting for."– With files from CBC Calgary

articles.title: Houthi missile attack on Yemeni presidential palace kills two, minister says
articles.summary: Yemen's information minister says the prime minister and other ministers were unhurt when ballistic missiles hit al-Maashiq Palace.

blocks.text: Two security personnel have been killed in a Houthi missile attack targeting the presidential palace in the port city of Aden in southern Yemen, which is the seat of the internationally-recognised government, officials say.
Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani told the BBC that the prime minister and other ministers were unhurt when five ballistic missiles hit al-Maashiq Palace, but that many others were injured.
The Houthis' military spokesman, Yahya Sarea, said they struck "the Saudi enemy's military operations headquarters in Aden".
A coalition led by Saudi Arabia backs the government and is providing air support for an offensive by pro-government forces against the Iran-backed Houthis.
Yemeni Prime Minister Shaya Zindani condemned the Houthis' attack on Aden, calling it "cowardly" and a "continuation of their criminal behaviour".

He said the government continued to carry out its duties and vowed that it would not weaken the resolve of its forces to continue operations against the Houthis on Yemen's south-western Red Sea coast and other front lines.

Earlier, the Houthis denied that they had attacked Saudi Arabia on Thursday, after the coalition said its forces had intercepted a cruise missile in the Medina region, home to one of Islam's holiest shrines.

The Houthis have been launching missiles and drones at airports, oil and gas facilities, and military bases in Saudi Arabia in retaliation for the strikes on the territory that they control in western Yemen, including the capital Sanaa.
On Saturday, a Houthi missile strike killed 13 people at Riyadh's international airport, which was the deadliest attack in Saudi Arabia in more than a decade.
Saudi Arabia's deputy foreign minister accused Iran of encouraging the Houthis to escalate their conflict with the kingdom.
"Iran continues to arm, train and support the Houthi militia in violation of UN Security Council resolutions," Rayed Krimly told reporters, according to AFP news agency.
"We think that the escalation by the Houthis at this latest stage of the conflict is encouraged by Iran," he added.
There was no immediate response from Iran's government. However, it has previously denied supplying weapons to the Houthis and said it only supports them politically.
Iran's foreign minister has also said it is ready to provide "any assistance necessary to facilitate the start of talks" between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis.

Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the internationally-recognised government from Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition of Arab states intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule.

A four-year-old informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.
The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they call a Saudi blockade of their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom.

The conflict escalated in September after the Houthis seized part of Yemen's south-western Red Sea coast near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a chokepoint for global shipping. Their advance contributed to a rise in oil prices following six months of war between the US, Israel and Iran.
Last week, pro-government forces said they had regained control of territory overlooking Bab al-Mandab after launching a major counter-offensive with the support of Saudi air strikes.
At least 1,282 people have been killed and 5,890 injured in the fighting in Yemen since 6 August, according to the government's health ministry.
The UN says another 201,000 people have been displaced and that there has been an alarming surge in suspected cholera cases.

articles.title: Thames Water asks for £2.4bn more to avoid going bust this year or early 2027
articles.summary:
Water company tells creditors it will not survive long enough to agree refinancing deal without more money

Thames Water has asked its creditors for another £2.4bn as the embattled water…

blocks.text: Thames Water has asked its creditors for another £2.4bn as the embattled water company comes close to running out of cash.

The UK’s largest water company said on Thursday it needed another short-term cash injection because it would be unable to reach a longer-term deal to sort out its giant debt pile before running out of cash by “the end of 2026 or the start of 2027”.

Thames Water said in a statement to the stock market that it “does not expect to complete its recapitalisation process ahead of this date”, meaning it would run out of cash without creditors stumping up more.

The utility company serves 16 million customers in London and the Thames valley. However, it has been on the brink of collapse for several years after it became overwhelmed by a debt pile that is now about £20bn. Its shareholders walked away, leaving the company under the effective control of its creditors while they work out a deal to avoid bankruptcy.

The creditors gave Thames a £3bn lifeline in February last year to try to see it through negotiations on a deal to cut its debts and inject more money. The creditors, collectively called the London & Valley Water company, are led by a group of American hedge funds such as Elliott Management and Silver Point Capital, and institutional investors including BlackRock and M&G.

However, those talks have dragged on, and the water company has now drawn down £2.65bn of the £3bn, leaving it perilously close to running out of cash even as it carries out a series of expensive repairs and upgrades.
Thames said the extra cash would “extend […] liquidity into autumn 2027 and allow [it] to continue to deliver its capital programme and deliver improvements for customers and the environment”.

Thames Water’s creditors have drawn up detailed proposals for a rescue plan that would involve them writing off £9.6bn in loans. However, that plan hinges on Ofwat agreeing to let the company pay set penalties for several years upfront, and effectively creating a special regime for the company. That prospect has proven politically unpalatable for the Labour government.

Some Labour politicians and environmental campaigners called on Keir Starmer and then Andy Burnham to put Thames Water into special administration, a form of temporary government control while a new buyer is sought.
Burnham has pledged more public control of the UK’s water industry, and has said that public ownership for Thames Water “is what should be done”.
after newsletter promotion

In addition, the change of prime minister has led to regulatory uncertainty for the broader water industry. Starmer’s government had committed to implementing recommendations on changes to the water system from the former Bank of England deputy governor Sir John Cunliffe, but Burnham’s government has not yet made clear what it plans to do.
Thames Water said it “continues to work closely with stakeholders to secure a market-led solution”.
Thames Water’s creditors are expected to vote on the proposals later in the month.

articles.title: Maduro pleads not guilty to new torture-related charges in New York
articles.summary: "I reject this document entirely," Maduro said in court, responding to newly added torture-related charges.

blocks.text: Venezuela's former leader Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, appeared in court on Thursday to plead not guilty to new charges of conspiracy to commit torture.
The US government initially accused Maduro of narco-terrorism, drug trafficking and weapons-related offenses, before adding new charges against him and Flores last week.
Maduro and Flores were captured in January during a US military raid, after which they were taken to New York, where they remain in jail.
The couple has pleaded not guilty to the allegations and both have argued to have the case thrown out on the grounds that they qualify for sovereign immunity. Their trial is scheduled for June 2027.

In a new indictment last week, government prosecutors alleged Maduro and Flores "created and maintained a violent system of repression" that saw "thousands of Venezuelans" killed, harassed, and tortured.
Nicolas Maduro denied the new charges brought against him by the US government, telling a court on Thursday he denied the "false accusations and false testimony against me."
"I reject this document entirely," Maduro said in Spanish through a translator.
Judge Alvin Hellerstein interrupted Maduro, and declared the court would enter a plea of not guilty for Maduro.
"I am completely innocent. I am not guilty," Flores said through a translator.
Maduro and Flores wore beige jail uniforms and both appear to have lost weight during their detention in Brooklyn.
The alleged torture methods included "electric shock, asphyxiation, rape, forced nudity, prolonged isolation, starvation, punishment cells, and psychological torture", the indictment states.
The US also accused Maduro of authorising the use of torture "against specific individuals" and alleges US citizens were tortured under this system.
Prosecutors already have accused Maduro, his wife and son, and their accomplices of engaging in a cocaine-trafficking conspiracy and partnering with cartels designated as terrorist groups.
Maduro previously called such charges a tool to further "imperial" plans for getting access to Venezuela's rich oil reserves.
He and his wife's lawyers have argued that Maduro is the leader of a sovereign country and therefore immune from prosecution. They contend the US taking him by force is illegal.

Flores unsuccessfully petitioned a judge to allow her to be released on bond while she awaited trial, arguing she had heart problems and other health issues while detained at the notorious Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn.

articles.title: 'Crypto King' tells court he fears he might soon end up in jail cell with his kidnappers
articles.summary: Self-described "Crypto King" Aiden Pleterski blamed his kidnapping for the fact he's currently representing himself at his fraud and money laundering trial in a victim impact statement he read at the…

image.caption: Self-described 'Crypto King' Aiden Pleterski, seen before entering court last week, read his victim impact statement at the sentencing submissions hearing for his kidnapper in Superior Court in Toronto on Thursday. (Evan Mitsui/CBC)

blocks.text: Toronto

Self-described "Crypto King" Aiden Pleterski blamed his kidnapping for the fact he's currently representing himself at his fraud and money laundering trial in a victim impact statement he read at the sentencing submissions for his kidnapper in Superior Court in Toronto on Thursday.
Aiden Pleterski read his victim impact statement in sentencing of kidnapper Thursday

Self-described "Crypto King" Aiden Pleterski blamed his kidnapping for the fact he's currently representing himself at his own trial in a victim impact statement he read at the sentencing submissions hearing for his kidnapper on Thursday.

"I have had to forego any normal routines, like having a steady job, as a safety precaution, which has spiralled into significant financial difficulties which have had far reaching consequences," said Pleterski in Superior Court in Toronto.
"The most significant is my inability to pay for a lawyer to defend me against the false allegations that this individual and others have made against me."

Pleterski's jury trial is currently underway in the same courthouse. He's pleaded not guilty to fraud over $5,000 and money laundering. So far Pleterski has only cross-examined the first of a dozen witnesses called by the Crown.

items: Real estate developer testifies he gave 'Crypto King’ Aiden Pleterski $4.5M to invest
'Crypto King' investor recounts the moment he learned $311M investment fund didn’t exist

blocks.text: Deren Akyeam-Pong pleaded guilty to nine charges related to Pleterski's 2022 kidnapping in October of last year. Those charges include kidnapping, assault and various gun charges.
This photo of Pleterski during his December 2022 kidnapping was entered as an exhibit during the guilty plea of his kidnapper Deren Akyeam-Pong. (Ontario Superior Court)

Pleterski, now 27, thought he was meeting with a potential investor on Dec. 5, 2022, when a gun was pressed into his ribs in the backseat of a pickup truck in Toronto. The abduction was the beginning of a three-day-long kidnapping during which Pleterski was threatened and tortured.

The torture included waterboarding, cigarette burns and getting beaten with golf clubs as his captors drove him between several locations in southern Ontario, according to the agreed statement of facts from Akyeam-Pong's guilty plea.
Three other men have also been charged in Pleterski's kidnapping. Their trial is expected to start later this year.
'Cannot sleep at night': Pleterski
"The thought that I may soon end up sharing a jail cell with my kidnappers has completely debilitated my ability to think clearly through this," read Pleterski in court Thursday.

"I cannot sleep at night. I come to court alone and am being asked to represent myself, but all I think about is being locked in a prison for an extended period of time with the same people who kidnapped, beat and threatened me."
Pleterski also spoke about the "emotional consequences" of his kidnapping, which he said are "difficult to explain to those who have not lived through it."
"Fear, stress, uncertainty and the continuing effort to process what happened consumes my thoughts and affects my well-being on a continuous basis."
The Crown in Pleterski's fraud and money laundering trial is alleging he spent investor money on himself, including on flights on private jets. (aiden_pletersik/Instagram)

The Crown in Pleterski's trial is alleging he guaranteed the money his investors gave him for trading, but never actually invested the funds. Instead, Crown prosecutor Scott Patterson argues Pleterski spent the money on himself, including on exotic cars, flights on private jets, lavish shopping and credit card bills that ran into the millions.

items: 'Crypto King' Aiden Pleterski spent investors' money on exotic cars, private jet flights: Crown

blocks.text: "Whatever opinions people may have of me, my financial affairs or the circumstances that preceded these events, no financial dispute justifies kidnapping, violence or intimidation," Pleterski said in his victim impact statement.

"Ultimately, I want to be able to move forward with my life without being defined by these events. I just hope that the time will come that I don't have to look over my shoulder or worry about the safety of my family."

Tracey Vogel, the Crown prosecutor in the kidnapping sentencing, is asking for a 23-year sentence for Akyeam-Pong related to the kidnapping conviction and a separate conviction for eight gun and drug-related offences.
Craig Zeeh, Akyeam-Pong's lawyer, is asking for a 12-year sentence. Sentencing submissions are expected to continue Thursday and Friday.
Pleterski's fraud trial is expected to continue Friday.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Nicole Brockbank is a reporter for CBC Toronto's Enterprise Unit. She digs up, researches and reports GTA-focused investigative and enterprise stories. nicole.brockbank@cbc.ca

articles.title: Police raid the major pro-opposition Halk TV channel in Turkey
articles.summary: Turkish police raided the Istanbul headquarters of an important pro-opposition television station on Wednesdazy, the day that jailed Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu was set to start his defense against…

image.caption: The police raided Halk TV in the middle of a live broadcast Image: Emrah Gurel/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: On Wednesday morning, the live broadcast was halted, Halk TV's headquarters in the city of Istanbul were searched, and a new administrator was appointed by the government to run the media outlet. An arrest warrant was issued for the station's CEO, Cafer Mahiroglu, who currently lives in London. According to prosecutors, 11 people were arrested.

Turkey has faced criticism for years over restrictions on press freedom. Halk TV is one of the country's best-known opposition television stations and regularly broadcasts critical reports about Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and his Justice and Development Party (AKP). After the raid, journalists were initially prevented from entering the building. Pre-recorded programs were broadcast instead of live reports.

The timing is particularly sensitive: Halk TV was raided on the very day that jailed Istanbul Mayor Ekrem İmamoglu was scheduled to begin his defense against corruption charges in court. The channel has been an important source of information for those following the trial.

Imamoglu, who won the mayoral election in Istanbul in 2019 and remained in office until his arrest on March 19, 2025, is one of Erdogan's most significant rivals, considered a beacon of hope for the opposition. He is still expected to run for president in 2028.

He is accused of establishing and running a criminal organization, as well as of various related financial crimes. Prosecutors are seeking a prison term of 2,352 years related to 142 charges. Imamoglu denies the allegations, arguing that the case is politically motivated.

blocks.caption: 11 people were arrested in conjunction with the raid on Halk TV headquarters Image: ANKA

blocks.text: Raid linked to investigation into Cafer Mahiroglu
Istanbul prosecutors said that the raid on Halk TV was linked to an investigation into its CEO Mahiroglu, who is accused of bribery, bid rigging and money laundering.

They said that arrest warrants had been issued for 17 people, on top of the 11 arrests. Assets belonging to companies allegedly linked to Mahiroglu were also seized and a trustee appointed to run the firms.
The opposition responded with sharp criticism of the police raid. Ozgur Ozel, the leader of the social democratic New Party (Yeni Parti) said it was a dark day for Turkey.
"The public's right to information is being seized for political reasons," Mahiroglu said.
"Showing solidarity with Halk TV means supporting the struggle for democracy in Turkey," Ozel said.

He added that "only dictators" would launch "a dawn raid on a television channel, appointing a trustee […]" and criticized the fact that this had occurred on the day that Imamoglu was due to begin his defense.

blocks.caption: Many people in Turkey protested in support of Ekrem Imamoglu when he was jailed in 2025, like here in Izmir on May 19, 2025Image: Berkcan Zengin/Middle East Images/picture alliance

blocks.text: Journalists' union slams raid
The Journalists' Union of Turkey (TGS) also condemned the raid on the platform X, describing it as arbitrary and arguing that the press was free and should not be censored.

Editor-in-chief Suat Toktas tried in vain to persuade the new state-appointed administrator to continue live broadcasts. In a video released by the TV channel, he said that what was happening was "illegal."
Halk TV began broadcasting on January 10, 2005 and its live broadcasts gained widespread attention particularly during the 2013 Gezi Park protests. Cafer Mahiroglu took over the station in 2020.
This article was translated from German.

articles.title: VP Sara should file case if she thinks Gracioso is lying --Matibag
articles.summary: National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag on Thursday said that Vice President Sara Duterte should file a case if she believes that dismissed policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. is…

blocks.text: Published October 16, 2026 12:41am

National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag on Thursday said that Vice President Sara Duterte should file a case if she believes that dismissed policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. is lying or that he is biased
“Kung may pagsisinungaling silang alegasyon kay Gracioso then file a case. Kung tingin nila ako ay nagiging bias or may mali akong ginagawa, file a case,” he said on Super Radyo dzBB.
(If they have false allegations against Gracioso, then file a case. If they think I am becoming biased or that I am doing something wrong, file a case.)

“Pero 'yung dudulog ka sa media, you will make an appeal on the emotion ng mga tao, magbibigay ng impormasyon na sasakyan ng mga troll para 'yun 'yung gawing atake, hindi 'yun ang katanggap-tanggap na behavior dapat,” he added.
(But if you go to the media, you will appeal to the emotions of the people, provide information that trolls will latch onto to use as an attack; that is not acceptable behavior.)

To recall, Gracioso alleged that he delivered cash to the vice president, Davao City 1st District Representative Paolo "Pulong" Duterte, and former President Rodrigo Duterte on former House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco’s instructions.
She has denied the allegations against her.

Matibag, meanwhile, said that the focus should now be on her alleged “underdeclared” properties.This comes amid the NBI’s probe into the real properties listed in the vice president’s Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALNs).
“We are way beyond the affidavit of Gracioso,” he said.
“Ang tanong na ngayon, ano ba itong mga properties na ito. Dineklara mo sa SALN, bakit underdeclared, tapos ngayon sasabihin, hindi ikaw yung may-ari,” he added.
(The question now is, what are these properties? You declared them in your SALN, so why were they underdeclared? Then now you’re saying you’re not the owner.)
Matibag said the investigation has been referred to the Office of the Ombudsman.
Meanwhile, Matibag addressed allegations by Duterte that the NBI was defending Gracioso.

“Well, to a certain extent na sasabihin pinoprotektahan, lahat ng tao, kailangan namin proteksyonan. Pero ano ba yung ibig sabihin ng pinoproteksyunan? Hindi na si Gracioso yung usapan dito, pinag-usapan natin dito, yung mga ari-arian,” Matibag said.

(Well, to a certain extent, when we are saying protection, we need to protect all people. But what does protection even mean? We are not just talking about Gracioso here, but the properties.) —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Nicolás Maduro tells New York court new torture allegations are ‘false’
articles.summary:
Rewritten indictment accuses ex-Venezuela president and wife Cilia Flores of leading campaign of torture

Nicolás Maduro insisted on Thursday during an appearance in a New York court that…

blocks.text: Nicolás Maduro insisted on Thursday during an appearance in a New York court that torture allegations in a rewritten drug trafficking indictment against the deposed Venezuelan president and his wife were “false accusations”.

Maduro, shackled at the ankles, was brought to court to face the new charges accusing the couple of leading a state-sponsored campaign of repression that tortured scores of victims, including three Americans.
Judge Alvin K Hellerstein entered a not-guilty plea on behalf of Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores. They were seized from their Caracas home by the US military in a night-time raid in January.

Hellerstein announced that he was entering the plea on behalf of Maduro after Maduro twice responded to the judge’s request to enter a plea by criticizing the indictment, saying it contained “false accusations and false testimony”. Maduro spoke through an interpreter.
Attorney Barry Pollack said when the charges were announced last week that Maduro, 63, denied them and “looks forward to his day in court”.

According to the rewritten indictment, Maduro oversaw a violent torture system that beat, asphyxiated and delivered electric shocks to its victims. He is accused of personally recommending torture methods, receiving updates on specific victims’ treatment and threatening to kill one prisoner’s child as a form of psychological torture.
Flores, 70, a former attorney general, helped develop the repressive system and ordered the torture of some specific people, the indictment alleges.
When she was asked to enter a plea, she said through an interpreter: “I am completely innocent. I am not guilty.”

Maduro, who served as Venezuela’s president from 2013 until his capture in January, has been under investigation for years by the international criminal court over allegations of crimes against humanity, tied to his crackdown on opponents. He has always denied wrongdoing.
Prosecutors told the judge during the hearing that lawyers on both sides want the trial date moved from 1 June to 14 June.

Torture is a crime under international law and can be prosecuted outside the country where the abuse occurred and regardless of the victims’ nationality. But the prosecution of foreign officials in the US is exceedingly rare, having been tried only a few times, including against the son of the former Liberian president Charles Taylor, Russians responsible for war crimes in Ukraine and a former prison warden in Bashar Assad’s Syria.

Earlier this year, Maduro and his wife pleaded not guilty in the US drug case, which said they conspired to flood the US with cocaine. Their attorneys say the case should be dismissed on immunity grounds because they were the leader and first lady of a foreign country.
The revised indictment covers allegations of torture stretching back to Maduro’s ascent to power in 2013, when he took over as president from his mentor Hugo Chávez, who died of cancer that year.

articles.title: School headscarf ban sparks rare protests in Azerbaijan and row with Turkey
articles.summary: Protests have taken place over the rules which have seen pupils wearing hijabs turned away from schools.

blocks.text: "You are telling me, I can't come to school?" says a teenage girl in a navy blue Islamic headscarf, captured on video challenging a staff member at the entrance to her school.
The footage has been shared widely on social media, and shows a group of girls in hijabs standing behind her applauding as she continues: "Why should I have to give up my religion?"

Last Monday the education ministry in Azerbaijan began enforcing new uniform rules, turning away female pupils wearing hijabs. Protests began outside state schools in the capital, Baku, and in several southern districts including Masally and Jalilabad.
Protests are rare in this oil- and gas-producing country of 10.5 million people.
Azerbaijan is constitutionally secular and the government strongly enforces that.
President Ilham Aliyev has been in power since 2003 and has little tolerance for dissent. Opposition politicians and many independent journalists are in jail.
Azerbaijan is pulled between two neighbours, Turkey and Iran. Azerbaijanis belong to a Turkic group of nations, speaking a language close to Turkish, and Turkey is its closest ally.
But like Iran to the south, Azerbaijan is mainly Shia - over 60% of its people identify as Shia Muslims, while most Turks are Sunni.
The interior ministry said it had detained 37 people on Monday who tried to obstruct the rules and "grossly violate public order".

Friends have also lost contact with Ilkin Huseynov, an activist who on Tuesday launched an online platform called "Let Leyli Go to School". It offers free lessons from volunteer teachers to pupils barred from class.
According to a friend, Huseynov left his home in Baku with unidentified men at about 16:00 on Wednesday, and his phone has been switched off ever since.
The authorities have not commented, but friends believe he has been detained. On Thursday, the platform's Instagram page could not be accessed.
Since the protests began, users have reported problems accessing Instagram and TikTok without a virtual private network (VPN).
Most of the protests have been in religiously conservative neighbourhoods in Baku's outlying settlements and in southern districts near the 765km (475-mile) border with Iran.
The authorities have long been wary of religious influence from Iran, where more ethnic Azerbaijanis live than in Azerbaijan itself.
On the night of 13 October, Azerbaijan's State Service for Special Communications and Information Security said a "foreign hacker group" had attacked more than 100 state websites.
A pro-Iranian group calling itself the 313 Team (Cyber Islamic Resistance) claimed responsibility.
Azerbaijani officials have defended the rules. One MP, Nigar Arpadarai, told the 1news.az website that children did not choose to wear the hijab themselves but were influenced by their families.
"A child has no freedom to choose a religion. This is a conscious prerogative of adults," she said.
The row has now spilled over into Turkey, Baku's closest ally, which provided vital support during Azerbaijan's 2020 war with Armenia over Nagorno-Karabakh.
The two countries call themselves "one nation, two states".
President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, a devout Muslim, has spoken of creating a "pious generation".
His chief adviser, Oktay Saral, has called the Azerbaijani restrictions "unacceptable" and urged Baku to "reverse this mistake".
"A headscarf is not an obstacle; it is a requirement of one's faith!" Saral wrote on X.
Several MPs from Turkey's governing AK Party joined in.

Small demonstrations were held outside Azerbaijan's embassy in Ankara, organised by Köklü Değişim, an Islamist movement linked to Hizb ut-Tahrir, and outside its consulate in Istanbul, organised by conservative Islamist group Özgür-Der.

President Aliyev's New Azerbaijan Party accused Turkish officials of an "openly defamatory" information campaign and of "baseless accusations", warning that Oktay Saral's comments risked harming ties, and cautioned against interference in Azerbaijan's internal affairs.
Earlier this month, Ilham Aliyev himself said no one should "stick their noses into our way of life".

Behind the dispute there may lie another source of friction. Turkish protesters have linked the headscarf rules to Azerbaijan's close ties with Israel, which sells weapons to Baku and buys Azerbaijani oil.
Turkey's relations with Israel have collapsed over Gaza, but Azerbaijan has tried to maintain relationships with both countries.

That is a difficult balancing act. On Thursday, when Israel's President Isaac Herzog addressed a regional security summit hosted by Azerbaijan in Baku, delegations from Turkey, Iran and other countries walked out of the hall.

articles.title: EXPLAINER: What is the Magna Carta for Persons with Disability
articles.summary: Under Republic Act No. 9442 or the Magna Carta for Persons with Disability, public ridicule and vilification against PWDs are strictly prohibited.

blocks.text: Published October 16, 2026 12:13am
A podcast show was recently terminated after its hosts made disparaging remarks about Kris Aquino's son, Josh, and his disability.
The network issued a statement apologizing for the remarks in the now-deleted Machong Chismisan post as it garnered an uproar online.
TV Host Boy Abunda condemned the remarks, describing them as cruel and hurtful to Josh and other people with disabilities (PWDs) and their families.

Meanwhile, child protection specialist Ace Diloy told GMA News Online that as much the public enjoys their right to freedom of speech, they should also exercise their humanity and emphasize with the vulnerable sectors.
Under Republic Act No. 9442 or the Magna Carta for Persons with Disability, public ridicule and vilification against PWDs are strictly prohibited.
The law amended to RA No. 7277 or the Magna Carta for Disabled Persons.

RA 9442 defined public ridicule as an "act of making fun or contemptuous initiating or making mockery of persons with disability whether in writing or in words, or in action due to their impairment/s."

"No individual, group or community shall execute any of these acts of ridicule against persons with disability in any time and place which could intimidate or result in loss of self-esteem of the latter," the law stated.
Meanwhile, the amended measure defined vilification as an utterance of slanderous and abusive statements against, or inciting hatred toward or severe ridicule of, a PWD.
"Any individual, group or community is hereby prohibited from vilifying any person with disability which could result into loss of self-esteem of the latter," the law stated.
A person found committing such prohibited acts will face a fine of P5,000 to P100,000 or imprisonment for six months to two years, or both.
Repeat offenders will be fined P100,000 to P200,000 or imprisonment of two to six years, or both.
If the violator is a corporation, organization or any similar entity, its officials directly involved will be liable.
If the violator is a foreigner, they will be deported immediately after serving their prison sentence without further deportation proceedings.

Upon filing a complaint and after proper notice and hearing, authorities may cancel or revoke the business permit, operating permit, franchise, or other privileges of any business that violates the said measure.
— BAP, GMA News

articles.title: Poll: Inflation, corruption top concerns of Pinoys
articles.summary: More than four years into the Marcos administration, reducing the basic cost of goods remains the most urgent concern of most Filipinos, based on a recent survey conducted by Pulse Asia.

blocks.text: October 16, 2026 | 12:00am
Results of the Sept. 17 to 24 survey released yesterday found that 71 percent of the respondents considered inflation as among the three most urgent national concerns of the respondents.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — More than four years into the Marcos administration, reducing the basic cost of goods remains the most urgent concern of most Filipinos, based on a recent survey conducted by Pulse Asia.
It went up by 14 percentage points from 57 percent in a similar survey conducted in July.
Reacting to the survey results, Malacañang assured the nation efforts are being made to fight hunger.
“These interventions are continuously being undertaken by the government,” Palace press officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said at a media briefing.

“If some of our countrymen are not yet covered by the assistance of the government, we would want to know where they are located so we can assess the situation, determine what is lacking and identity the assistance we can provide,” she added.
Based on the survey, controlling inflation was ranked first by 36 percent of the respondents, the largest proportion among issues included in the poll.
It was also the issue selected by most respondents across geographic areas and socio-economic classes.
Meanwhile, 39 percent of the respondents identified graft and corruption as among their top three concern. It went down from 43 percent in July.

Other top issues included in the survey were increasing the pay of workers (36 percent), fighting criminality (24 percent), reducing poverty (21 percent), creating more jobs (18 percent), fighting the widespread sale and use of illegal drugs (18 percent) and lowering the price of gasoline (14 percent).

Selected by less than 10 percent of the respondents were issues such as providing assistance to farmers, promoting peace, addressing hunger, equal enforcement of the law, reducing taxes, responding to needs of areas affected by calamities, stopping the destruction of the environment, providing support to small businesses, defending the integrity of Philippine territory, protecting overseas workers and preparing to face any kind of terrorism.
The survey had 2,400 respondents and a margin of error of plus/minus two percent.

articles.title: PCC slaps P1.76 billion fine on 2022 onion cartel
articles.summary: The Philippine Competition Commission has imposed a record fine of P1.76 billion on six firms whose activities as an onion cartel sent retail prices soaring to as high as P800 a kilo in 2022.

blocks.text: October 16, 2026 | 12:00am

At a press conference yesterday, PCC executive director Kenneth Tanate said the fine was imposed on the six firms and their officers for their involvement in an illegal market allocation scheme in the importation, cold storage and wholesale distribution of onions.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine Competition Commission (PCC) has imposed a record fine of P1.76 billion on six firms whose activities as an onion cartel sent retail prices soaring to as high as P800 a kilo in 2022.
The scheme allowed the firms to control nearly 50 percent of all import clearances for onions.
The PCC issued its decision on Oct.1. The firms have until today to pay the fine.
“The members of the cartel were fined a total of P1.76 billion, representing the biggest amount imposed so far by the Philippine Competition Act (PCA) on violators of the law,” he said.
As onion is classified as a prime commodity, he said the PCA mandates automatic trebling or tripling the penalty.

Fined were freight forwarder Golden Shine International Freight Forwarders Corp., cold storage operator Tian Long Corp., and onion importers La Reina Fresh Vegetables & Young Indoor Plants Inc. and Yom Trading Corp.

Also penalized were Mark Castro Ocampo as sole proprietor of Vegefru Producing Store, Nancy Callanta Rosal as sole proprietor of Rosal Fruit and Vegetable Trading, Golden Shine president Lilia Cruz, Golden Shine corporate executive officer and Tian Long corporate secretary Eric Pabilona, La Reina and Yom Trading chairman and president Renato Francisco Jr., and Golden Shine incorporator Letty Baculando.
The PCC’s decision stemmed from an investigation on surge in onion prices to as high as P800 a kilo in late 2022.

Evidence retrieved during a court-ordered dawn raid conducted in September 2023 revealed how the cartel operated. Base on investigation, Golden Shine applied for import clearances using the other importers’ credentials and assigned the same importers as consignees. Imports were routed to Tian Long’s cold storage facilities and then distributed nationwide.
Tanate said the firms may file a motion for reconsideration.
The fines were calculated using actual import clearance volumes and wholesale prices reported by the Philippine Statistics Authority as the firms understated financial performance.

“By imposing the maximum fines, the PCC underscores its commitment to holding cartels accountable across all sectors of the economy and protecting consumers from the harmful effects of anti-competitive conduct,” Tanate said.
Aside from imposing administrative penalties, the PCC may recommend a criminal case before the Department of Justice.

articles.title: China envoy urges dialogue on West Philippine Sea tensions
articles.summary: Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan has urged the Philippines to exercise caution in discussing its maritime dispute with his country, calling for face-to-face dialogues to manage tensions as officials and…

blocks.text: October 16, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan has urged the Philippines to exercise caution in discussing its maritime dispute with his country, calling for face-to-face dialogues to manage tensions as officials and analysts pushed for stronger regional cooperation during a forum in Quezon City.

“Through communication and dialogues, we find ways to manage disputes,” Jing said at the second Diliman Dialogues hosted by Diliman College, titled “Southeast Asian Voices on China-ASEAN Relations: Pathways to Peace in the South China Sea.”

Jing acknowledged the complexity of Manila-Beijing relations, saying they could not simply be described as good or bad. He urged both sides to separate areas of disagreement from other aspects of their relationship and encouraged more exchanges.

“We should encourage the two sides to visit each other more and sit face to face,” he said, adding that the Philippines should maintain balanced relations with China, the United States and other countries.

National security experts and lawmakers at the forum also stressed the need for dialogue, but emphasized that cooperation should protect Philippine interests and support a rules-based approach to the maritime dispute.

Former national security adviser Clarita Carlos said the Philippines should pursue multilateralism without becoming beholden to any country while House special committee on the West Philippine Sea chairman Antolin Oreta III said the dispute was not only about territory but also about upholding the law.

Philippines-China Studies Center director Rommel Banlaoi said Manila should maintain diplomatic balance and pursue cooperation in areas of mutual benefit, which could help create conditions for resolving maritime disputes.

Meanwhile, Association for Philippines-China Understanding chairman Raul Lambino called for greater cooperation in technology, energy and food security, maintaining that partnerships with neighboring countries could support national development.

Diliman College president and CEO Anna Dominique Coseteng, however, cautioned against rhetoric that could deepen distrust, saying national security concerns should not fuel prejudice against Filipino-Chinese communities.
But while Beijing’s ambassador was calling for caution, the Philippine Coast Guard was driving away Chinese fishing boats from Lawak Island.
According to the PCG, four small boats were reportedly deployed by the Chinese fishing vessel Yuetaiyu 63168 when it anchored within the territorial sea of the island.
Lawak Island is a Philippine-occupied feature in the West Philippine Sea. It is part of the Kalayaan municipality in Palawan.
PCG spokesman for the West Philippine Sea Rear Adm. Jay Tarriela said the Chinese vessels ignored repeated radio challenges but eventually left.
Meanwhile, Tarriela slammed the Chinese ambassador’s statement that Beijing “may easily win” if it chooses to use force against the Philippines in the West Philippine Sea.
In a chance interview, Quan said the Philippines is “fortunate to have a neighbor like China” which does not use force to address the tensions in the area.
“A guest who reminds his host that he could easily beat him up, but has graciously decided not to, is not describing friendship,” Tarriela said.

At the recent South China Sea International Conference in Hanoi, Vietnam, the Philippines underscored the importance of upholding the rule of law and strengthening maritime cooperation in addressing emerging challenges to the regional maritime order.
The conference brought together over 300 participants composed of government officials, policymakers, maritime experts, academics among other stakeholders.

Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) Undersecretary Leo Herrera-Lim said unilateral actions beyond what is permitted under international law, as well as coercive conduct, have heightened risks for coastal states.
Herrera-Lim emphasized that, for the Philippines, lasting peace and prosperity at sea can rest on nothing other than the rule of law.

The 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) and the final and binding 2016 South China Sea Arbitral Award, he said, serve as the twin anchors of Philippine maritime policy. – Pia Lee-Brago, Andrew Ronquillo

articles.title: Pulse: VP Sara ratings still higher than Marcos Jr’s
articles.summary: Even with the ongoing impeachment trial against her, Vice President Sara Duterte continues to enjoy much higher trust and approval ratings than President Marcos, a survey for the third quarter…

blocks.text: October 16, 2026 | 12:00am
Vice President Sara Duterte and President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — Even with the ongoing impeachment trial against her, Vice President Sara Duterte continues to enjoy much higher trust and approval ratings than President Marcos, a survey for the third quarter conducted by Pulse Asia showed.
The survey conducted from Sept. 17 to 24 found that 29 percent of the respondents trust the President, almost similar to the 28 percent he obtained in a similar survey in July.
Those who distrusted him fell from 51 percent to 48 percent, while undecided respondents hardly changed, from 21 percent to 22 percent.
Marcos had an approval rating of 30 percent, from 29 percent, and a disapproval rating of 49 percent, from 50 percent. Undecided respondents were unchanged at 21 percent.
Unlike Marcos, Duterte retained a majority trust and approval ratings.
Those who said they trust her dropped from 58 percent to 55 percent, while those who distrust her remained at 27 percent. Undecided respondents increased from 16 percent to 19 percent.

In terms of approval, Duterte obtained a rating 54 percent, down from 56 percent. Her disapproval rating also dropped from 29 percent to 27 percent, while undecided respondents increased from 15 percent to 18 percent.
The Pulse Asia survey was conducted amid the ongoing impeachment trial of Duterte at the Senate. It had 2,400 respondents and a margin of error of plus/minus two percent.

The Office of the Vice President (OVP) gave away P5.16 million worth of medical and burial assistance in 2025 from its own budget, which is more than 99 percent lower than the P820.77 million it distributed in 2024, according to a report by the Commission on Audit (COA).

Based on the OVP’s financial statements attached to COA’s audit report, the agency was able to distribute medical and burial assistance worth P59.936 million in 2025, but this was sourced from donation in cash from the Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corp. (Pagcor).
In the previous years, the OVP distributed P29.93 million cash assistance for medical and burial purposes from the same Pagcor donations.

Funding for the medical and burial assistance program of the OVP was removed in the 2025 national budget after COA flagged unexplained confidential fund expenditures involving millions in a matter of days.
Lawmakers had proposed cutting the funding for the OVP’s social welfare projects as it overlapped with programs of the Department of Health and the Department of Social Welfare and Development.
The OVP received appropriations totaling P2.448 billion in 2023, P1.898 billion in 2024, and P766.146 million in 2025. - Daphne Galvez

“The money was in the suitcases, already bundled. You can smell new money. I am disgusted by the smell,” Orbillo told the court. He added that he had also delivered money to Romualdez in three other properties linked to the lawmaker.

articles.title: Amendments to ‘archaic’ anti-espionage law sought
articles.summary: To strengthen the country’s defense against modern security threats, Senate President Pro Tempore Vicente Sotto III has pushed for the amendment of the country’s outdated anti-espionage…

blocks.text: October 16, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — To strengthen the country’s defense against modern security threats, Senate President Pro Tempore Vicente Sotto III has pushed for the amendment of the country’s outdated anti-espionage law.
Sotto raised his proposal at the hearing yesterday of the Senate committee on national defense and security, peace, unification and reconciliation.

He said the existing laws were antiquated and crafted for traditional wartime threats, not peacetime threats like foreign interference, cyberattacks and the illegal disclosure of sensitive government information.

“In today’s rapidly changing world, national security is no longer threatened only by traditional warfare. Espionage, cyber attacks, the theft of confidential information, and the illegal sharing of sensitive government data pose serious risks to the safety, sovereignty, and independence of the Philippines,” he said.

“This is why the Philippines’ anti-espionage and foreign interference laws should be updated. Our laws must keep pace with modern technology, emerging security threats, and the changing methods used by foreign intelligence operations,” Sotto added.
He explained that the existing laws “may leave gaps that can be exploited making it more difficult to protect our national interest and hold offenders accountable.”
The Senate is eyeing the passage of a more stringent anti-espionage law because the current 1941 legislation is archaic and can only be enforced during wartime.
Senators also pressed the need for stronger anti-espionage laws to crack down on spies from China amid the West Philippine Sea issue.

articles.title: Refuting dropped raps vs Sara a waste of time– prosecutors
articles.summary: The decision to withdraw three of the four Articles of Impeachment against Vice President Sara Duterte was meant to expedite the proceedings, the prosecution panel of the House of Representatives…

blocks.text: October 16, 2026 | 12:00am
(From L) Impeachment defense counsels Sheila Sison and Michael Poa, lead prosecutor Rep. Jinky Luistro, Sen. Pia Cayetano and presiding officer Chiz Escudero and private prosecutor Lorna Kapunan.
Senate SMU / Joseph Vidal

MANILA, Philippines — The decision to withdraw three of the four Articles of Impeachment against Vice President Sara Duterte was meant to expedite the proceedings, the prosecution panel of the House of Representatives said yesterday.

House legal spokesman Benjamin Tolosa Jr. explained that their objective was to make the impeachment process faster, and allow their counterparts to focus on one charge alone – the P1.5 billion unexplained wealth of the Vice President and her husband Manases Carpio.

“The ruling of the (impeachment) court is that the issues now will be confined to those relating to the unexplained wealth and the evidence that should be presented, should be confined to that,” he explained.

Refuting the dropped articles “will be a complete waste of time and resources of the court and everyone involved,” Tolosa maintained, as he rejected the proposed middle ground of allowing Duterte’s lawyers to answer evidence already presented under the abandoned charges.

The Senate impeachment court allowed prosecutors to withdraw the confidential funds, bribery and grave threats articles and limited the remaining defense presentation to Article II on alleged unexplained wealth.

Duterte’s lawyers have argued that fairness requires allowing them to counter evidence and testimony already heard publicly under the withdrawn articles even if the senator-judges will no longer vote on those charges.
Not a waste
Malacañang yesterday rejected criticism that the prosecution had wasted time and taxpayers’ money when it withdrew three articles of impeachment against Duterte.
“It cannot be claimed that there was wastage if there are facts, data that can provide explanation to the people,” Palace press officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said.
Asked about the defense team raising the possibility of a mistrial, Castro said such a scenario may be declared if the other party was not given any chance to present evidence.

“They were given ample time and opportunities to cross-examine the witnesses presented by the prosecution. Again, the defense team did not make any objection regarding the motion to withdraw the three articles of impeachment,” she added.
Duterte’s defense team may only need five to 10 trial days to present its evidence on the remaining Article II.
“Because there is only one article that needs to be tackled when we resume on Nov. 9, so likely at most, between five to 10 trial days,” Barbers said.
The defense had earlier prepared its original witness list and requested trial dates when all four impeachment articles remained part of the case.

Barbers added that prosecutors were originally opposed to withdrawing the three Articles of Impeachment, precisely because they have already presented evidence for the two charges – grave threats and confidential funds.

“They were initially not sold to the idea during the discussions. Although of course when they were asked about the issue if they were open to the idea, what was their opinion? Of course, at first, they didn’t agree with it,” Barbers recalled.

“Actually, many have given their opinion. That is what’s good…” he said. “So, it was taken up. And you know, there was voting. So, most of the people in that meeting agreed to focus on the unexplained wealth.”

While the Vice President is willing to stand as a witness in her impeachment case, it would depend on the “trigger point,” meaning if only she knows the answers and could give an explanation, defense panel spokesman Michael Poa told ANC, when asked if Duterte would stand as a witness in the impeachment trial. – Alexis Romero, Daphne Galvez, Evelyn Macairan

articles.title: NBI chief dares VP: File case over properties probe
articles.summary: National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag is challenging Vice President Sara Duterte to file a case if she believes that the NBI is biased in its investigation on properties linked to…

blocks.text: October 16, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag is challenging Vice President Sara Duterte to file a case if she believes that the NBI is biased in its investigation on properties linked to her family.
Matibag insisted that the NBI inquiry is backed by official records and evidence.

“If they think I am biased, file a case,” Matibag said at a press briefing at the NBI headquarters yesterday as he responded to accusations that he was politically motivated in investigating the allegations raised by dismissed police officer Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. against the Vice President.
Matibag said the investigation had moved beyond Gracioso’s affidavit and is now focused on properties declared in Duterte’s statements of assets, liabilities and net worth (SALN).
“Why would you declare these properties in your SALN? Why are the transfer certificates of title numbers described in your SALN?” Matibag said.

He said the NBI obtained copies of the titles from the Land Registration Authority (LRA), visited the properties based on their descriptions, conducted geotagging and interviewed residents to verify ownership.
“They were the ones who declared these properties. We did not create this evidence. They themselves declared that these were their properties,” he said.

Matibag cited an agricultural land in Catigan, Davao City, which he said was declared in Duterte’s SALN at a combined assessed value of about P890,000. He questioned the valuation after investigators documented the property.
“It is hardly acceptable that these properties are worth only P890,000,” he said, adding that the NBI had prepared a 79-page study detailing its validation process.
The NBI chief said the bureau forwarded its findings to the Office of the Ombudsman for appropriate action and would continue investigating other possible sources of funds and business links.

He said investigators are coordinating with the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) and are examining transactions involving corporations, including businessman Jaime T. Cruz, as well as funds from Cale88 and Pikimong Pikimong.

Matibag said the bureau was also looking into properties allegedly linked to other individuals, including former House speaker Lord Allan Velasco, and was handling more than 30 other flood control-related matters involving public officials.
He rejected claims that the investigation amounted to trial by publicity, saying the NBI was responding to matters of public interest and submitting evidence through established procedures.
“This is not trial by publicity. This is a matter of public interest,” he said. “We are looking at evidence, not personalities.”

Meanwhile, Matibag said the management of Casas Con Vistas Resort in Samal Island did not need to issue a statement denying ownership links to Davao City 1st district Rep. Paolo Duterte, saying the establishment was not the property identified in the NBI investigation.
Matibag clarified the issue, saying the resort had apparently been confused with a neighboring property allegedly linked to the congressman.

“There is no need for Casas Con Vistas to issue a statement because it was not the establishment being referred to, nor was it the property shown in the photographs. It is beside the property we were talking about,” Matibag said.
The resort management earlier denied social media reports claiming that Paolo Duterte or a government official had an ownership stake in the establishment.
Matibag said the NBI released photographs and videos of properties allegedly linked to members of the Duterte family as part of its investigation into possible discrepancies in their SALNs.
The Office of the Ombudsman, for its part, said it will conduct an impartial investigation on the alleged undeclared assets of the Vice President.
The anti-graft body issued the statement after receiving the referral from the NBI on the potential discrepancies in the Vice President’s SALNs.

“The referral and its supporting documents will undergo an initial evaluation to determine the appropriate action, including whether further investigation is warranted, in accordance with established procedures and applicable laws,” the Ombudsman said.
“The Office assures the public that the matter will be handled thoroughly, independently and without any political color,” it added. – Daphne Galvez

articles.title: Raul Daza, esteemed Northern Samar lawmaker, dies at 91
articles.summary: Former Speaker Pro Tempore Raul Aguila Daza, a longtime lawmaker and former governor of Northern Samar, died at 91, his family announced Thursday.

blocks.text: Published October 15, 2026 11:49pm
Former Speaker Pro Tempore Raul Aguila Daza, a longtime lawmaker and former governor of Northern Samar, died at 91, his family announced Thursday.

"It is with profound sadness that our family announces the passing of our beloved Raul Aguila Daza. He peacefully passed away at 91 years old," said a statement released by his grandson, Northern Samar Rep. Niko Raul Daza.
Daza devoted more than five decades to public service, serving seven terms in the House of Representatives from 1969 to 2019 and three terms as Northern Samar governor from 2001 to 2010.
He also served as senior deputy speaker of the House, deputy minister of the Presidential Commission on Good Government, and commissioner of the Presidential Commission on Constitutional Reforms.

A lawyer and certified public accountant, Daza graduated cum laude from the University of the Philippines College of Law and placed 11th in the Philippine Bar examinations. His family said he was believed to be the first Philippine-educated professional to pass both the California Bar and CPA examinations.
Daza was a longtime Liberal Party member, which he joined in 1965. He served as party president from 1994 to 1998 and later chaired the Council of Asian Liberals and Democrats.
His family described him as a "steadfast defender of democracy, justice and the rule of law" who stood by his convictions during martial law and political exile.

As governor and representative of Northern Samar, Daza helped lay the groundwork for the province's development, guided by his belief that communities long burdened by poverty could achieve greater opportunities and prosperity, the statement said.
“Despite the many colours of politics, he firmly believed that we have only one flag, and we have only one country,” his family said.
Wake details

Daza's wake will be held from Oct. 17 to 19 at The Chapels at Heritage Park in Taguig City. The Liberal Party will hold a tribute on Oct. 18 at 7 p.m., followed by a necrological service at the House of Representatives in Quezon City on Oct. 19.

His remains will then be brought to Catarman, Northern Samar, where services will be held at his residence and the provincial capitol gymnatorium from Oct. 21 to 24. A funeral Mass is scheduled for Oct. 24 at 1 p.m. at the Our Lady of Annunciation Cathedral in Catarman.

The family requested that mourners refrain from sending flowers and instead consider supporting the Foundation for the Diocese of Catarman, citing Daza's enduring concern for the people of Northern Samar.
Liberal Party stalwart

In a statement, the LP said, "Isa si Manong Raul Aguila Daza sa mga naging matatag na haligi ng Partido Liberal. Sa mahabang panahon ng kanyang paglilingkod at pakikibahagi sa ating partido, nanatili siyang bahagi ng kasaysayan at patuloy na paninindigan ng mga Liberal."
"Mula noon hanggang ngayon, si Manong Raul ay isa sa mga patunay ng diwang #HindiPasisiil—ang paninindigang hindi basta sumusuko sa mga hamon at patuloy na naglilingkod para sa bayan," it added.
ML Party-list Rep. Leila de Lima said Daza had been a "fatherly figure" throughout her journey in public service "and during the most challenging chapter of my life."

"Sa panahon ng aking di-makatarungang pagkakulong, hindi siya nakalimot. Bukod sa makailang beses siyang personal na bumisita sa akin, regular din siyang nangumusta, nagpadala ng mga libro, at mga sulat – nagpayo, nagsilbing gabay at nagpatatag ng aking loob na magpatuloy sa laban," she said.

"Higit sa pagiging maaasahang kapartido, tapat siya sa pagsisilbi sa ating mga kababayan. Sa mahabang panahon ng kanyang paglilingkod, nanatili ang kanyang integridad, malasakit at matapang na paninindigan," De Lima added. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Russia arrests Swedish national, claims he's Ukraine fighter
articles.summary: Russian intelligence agents have arrested a Swedish man they say led a Ukrainian drone unit. He was detained at Russia's western border and is accused of planning acts of terrorism and sabotage.

image.caption: Russia's FSB intelligence service released a video in which a Swedish man allegedly confessed to planning acts of terror in Russia on Ukraine's behalf Image: Russian State Media/REUTERS

blocks.text: Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) on Thursday announced the arrest and detention of a Swedish national that authorities say fights for Ukraine.
What do we know so far?
The 35-year-old Swede, detained near Pskov on Russia's western border, has been charged with illegally entering the country and may face additional terrorism charges, said FSB representatives.
Russia claims to have secured documents proving that the man led a Ukrainian drone unit.
They are now investigating whether he could be charged with organizing terror attacks on behalf of Ukraine or other Western intelligence services.

According to the FSB, the man "entered the Russian Federation under the pretext of joining the ranks of the Russian armed forces with the aim of carrying out acts of sabotage and terrorist attacks on military installations."
The FSB also released a video that it claimed showed the man confessing that he had entered Russia to commit "terrorist attacks" and sabotage.
Putin on a war footing: escalation on all fronts?

During the video the man spoke in English, saying that he was from Stockholm, had signed a contract with Ukraine's Defense Ministry and had received drone training. Russian state TV showed images of what it said was the man's contract with Ukraine.
The Pskov region borders Belarus, Estonia and Latvia — the latter two being EU and NATO member states — FSB officials did not specify where exactly the man had arrived from.
Sweden aware of incident, with no comment yet from Ukraine
The Swedish Foreign Ministry has said that it is aware of the situation but not involved.
Ukraine has not commented on the arrest.
On Tuesday, Russia arrested a Japanese journalist that Moscow accused of spying, a claim that Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi rejected.

Russia itself has been accused of hiring and deploying numerous individuals to commit acts of sabotage abroad or to recruit locals willing to do so — this, beyond the country's legions of malign cyber actors.
None of the claims made by Russia and the FSB on Thursday can be substantiated.
